home.badge: Learn git the way it actually works
home.subtitle: No more memorizing incantations. Each command gets a plain-English explanation, an animated look at what happens to objects, refs and HEAD under the hood — and the real-world aliases the pros type every day.
home.mentalTitle: Four things. That's the whole engine.
home.mentalSubtitle: Everything git does is a dance between objects, refs, the index and HEAD. Commit to these four and every command below becomes obvious.

fundamentals.title: Objects
fundamentals.desc: Every blob, tree, commit and tag is an immutable, content-addressed object stored in .git/objects. Nothing is ever edited — history only grows.

fundamentals.title: Refs
fundamentals.desc: A ref is just a file holding one commit hash — a name for a position in history. Branches and tags are the same thing with different rules for moving.

fundamentals.title: The Index
fundamentals.desc: Also called the staging area, .git/index holds your next commit: path → blob-hash pairs. It lets you build a snapshot before you take it.

fundamentals.title: HEAD
fundamentals.desc: A file that says which branch you're on. When you commit, reset, or switch, HEAD (and the branch it points to) is what moves.

home.mapBannerTitle: See how they connect in the command map
home.mapBannerDesc: Every command plotted against the places it touches — working tree, index, repository and remote.
home.libraryTitle: Every command, grouped by the job it does.
home.ctaSubtitle: Open one command page and watch its objects, refs and pointers move right in front of you — then memorize it forever with an alias.
home.scenarioTitle: Watch a real, human day of git
home.scenarioDesc: Sixteen guided steps: scaffold the repo, split a messy session into atomic commits with chore / feat / style prefixes, and ship a feature on a branch — the 50/72 way, not the 50-files-in-one-commit way.

notFound.title: This commit doesn't exist.
notFound.body: A stray ref, a force-push, a typo — something pointed here and got rewound. The reflog of life keeps no record of this page.

scenario.title: One real day of git. Done like a human.
scenario.subtitle: A work/play walkthrough of a realistic session — small atomic commits, conventional prefixes, and a clean story. No 50-file blobs, no lazy "update" messages.
scenario.ruleBody: Subject under 50 characters, detail wrapped at 72. If a change needs more than one paragraph, it deserves its own commit.
scenario.whyBody: An atomic commit is one logical change — easy to review, easy to revert, easy to cherry-pick. A 50-file mega-commit is a black box nobody dares to touch.
